<reason>B won by making the live choice easier: consent is either a checkbox, a de facto ban, or a market in leftover unjustified surveillance, while necessity/limits already do the real work. A was vivid on coercion and necessity-creep, but had to carve bank logs out of the motion’s own keystroke rule and never made the equal-promotions floor auditable. Two clipped B turns are a real cost, yet not enough to offset B’s cleaner comparative map.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s use of A’s “if fraud detection needs a log, collect the log” against the motion’s opt-in text, then treating A’s later scoped-log carve-out as abandoning the proposition.</best_rebuttal>
